> Why can't i Bleed my Predator for 1 pool for example, and i can
> call a Parity Shift to transfer 5 pool from him?
> (I want to know what is the logic behind it.)

(Unsure of exactly what angle you're taking here, so multiple
answers follow.)

You can bleed your predator for 1 pool. Use Night Moves or
Cat Burglary, for example.

Just like Parity Shift has card text allowing you to choose a
Methuselah who is not your prey to lose pool, a bleed action
card can that includes the appropriate text can allow you to
bleed a Methuselah who is not your prey.

A "bleed" is an action that is directed at your prey by default
(see the description of "bleed" in the rulebook).

Explicit card text is needed to change that default.
As a tangent: All bleeds are directed, so mentioning that a
bleed is directed (by including a "(D)" symbol in card text, for
instance) isn't sufficient.

One reason why you can only bleed your prey by default is to
limit the "king-maker" effect - of giving someone (typically
someone who finds herself in a losing position) to easily
choose which of the other players will win (by bleeding that
chosen player's prey). By requiring a card to affect a
non-prey Methuselah (w/ Parity Shift or Night Moves, for
instance), the "king-maker" effect is reduced.

> Is it "political" correct to call a KRC to burn Methuselah's pool that
> are NOT my predator or prey (ie, cross-table)?

That is acceptable, sure.

Messages.Author: Richard Zopf
Messages.Body:
Luis P. Duarte wrote in message <37206...@news.ip.pt>...
>Hi all!

>
>Why can't i Bleed my Predator for 1 pool for example, and i can
>call a Parity Shift to transfer 5 pool from him?
>(I want to know what is the logic behind it.)
>

If the basic bleed action could be pointed at anyone, the predator/prey
relationship would become meaningless, and most games would likely devolve
into kingmaker type situations (ever play Diplomacy?). The reason why you
can't see the logic is also because you're comparing a simple bleed with a
vote. Voting successfully involves a LOT more than an action with a card,
as I'm sure you know (unblocked vote action, near or complete vote control,
or bribing of other voters at the table, etc.). The setup for successfully
calling a 5 pool loss to your predator with PS is equal to the effect it
generates.

>Is it "political" correct to call a KRC to burn Methuselah's pool that
>are NOT my predator or prey (ie, cross-table)?
>

There are no "correct" ways to call votes in Jyhad. There is only the
circumstance of the particular game you are in. You have to compare what
the vote will get you against what you have to sacrifice (and who you might
have to bribe to get the vote passed).

Regards,
